name: Yellowing leaves
description: Leaves lose their green color. Note whether old or new leaves are affected.

name: Brown leaf tips
description: Tips or edges turn brown, often with a dry border.

name: Drooping / wilting
description: Leaves hang limply or stems lose their usual firmness.

name: Falling leaves
description: Leaves drop more quickly than the plant normally sheds them.

name: Brown or black spots
description: Distinct dark patches appear on leaf surfaces.

name: White powder
description: A flour-like coating appears on leaf surfaces.

name: Sticky leaves
description: A tacky film or droplets coat leaves and nearby surfaces.

name: Tiny insects
description: Small moving insects, cottony clusters, or fixed bumps are visible.

name: Curling leaves
description: Leaf edges roll inward or young leaves emerge distorted.

name: Soft or mushy stems
description: Stems soften, darken, or collapse, especially near the soil.

name: Stunted growth
description: Little new growth appears during the active growing season.

name: Dry and crispy leaves
description: Leaves feel brittle and papery rather than soft.

name: Rotten-looking roots
description: Roots appear dark and mushy, with tissue that slips off.

name: Pale leaves
description: Foliage looks unusually light green or washed out.

name: Holes in leaves
description: New irregular holes or chewed edges appear; ignore normal Monstera splits.
